from tslearn.metrics.cysax import inv_transform_paa

# X2 has shape (4, 32, 1). We will treat it as a PAA representation 
# and reconstruct it to an original size of 64 (repeating each element twice).
original_size = X2.shape[1] * 2
dataset_out = inv_transform_paa(X2, original_size)

# Verify the output shape matches the requested original_size
assert dataset_out.shape == (X2.shape[0], original_size, X2.shape[2]), f"Unexpected shape: {dataset_out.shape}"

# Verify the inverse PAA logic: elements should be repeated to fill the original size
# For original_size = 2 * sz, each element is repeated exactly twice.
assert dataset_out[0, 0, 0] == X2[0, 0, 0]
assert dataset_out[0, 1, 0] == X2[0, 0, 0]
assert dataset_out[0, 2, 0] == X2[0, 1, 0]
assert dataset_out[0, 3, 0] == X2[0, 1, 0]

print(f"__CHECK__ inv_transform_paa {dataset_out.shape}")
